question: You are performing ABO blood grouping on a fresh blood specimen using the tile method. You add anti-A serum to one drop and anti-B serum to another. After two minutes, you observe: agglutination with anti-A only, no agglutination with anti-B. According to Landsteiner's Law, what are the blood group AND the expected serum antibodies in this person?

answers.text: Blood group A; serum contains anti-A and anti-B antibodies.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Landsteiner's Law states that if an antigen is absent from the red cell surface, the corresponding antibody will be present in the serum — but never against the antigen you possess. Group A has anti-B in serum, not anti-A.

answers.text: Blood group A; serum contains anti-B antibody only.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Agglutination with anti-A only = A antigen on red cells = Group A. Landsteiner's Law: Group A persons have anti-B (not anti-A) in their serum. This is consistent — you never form antibodies against your own antigens.

answers.text: Blood group B; serum contains anti-A antibody only.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Agglutination with anti-A serum means the red cells carry A antigen, which defines Group A, not Group B. Group B agglutinates with anti-B serum.

answers.text: Blood group AB; serum contains no ABO antibodies.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Group AB would agglutinate with BOTH anti-A and anti-B sera. Agglutination with anti-A only, and not anti-B, is the defining reaction for Group A.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review 'Governing Principles: ABO and Rh Blood Group Systems'. Landsteiner's Law: Group A → anti-B in serum; Group B → anti-A; Group AB → no ABO antibodies; Group O → both anti-A and anti-B. The serum antibody is always against the absent antigen.
Correct. Agglutination with anti-A only = Group A; serum has anti-B per Landsteiner's Law. You never produce antibodies against antigens on your own cells.
